title: First mortgage company authority
summary: Confirm the company has the authority required for its proposed first-mortgage activity. The statute distinguishes license, registration and exceptions.
evidence: Company authority, activities, exemption rationale if relevant, exact dates and source.
counsel: Which entity, activities and offices are in scope? Does any claimed exception apply?

title: Secondary mortgage company authority
summary: Evaluate the Secondary Mortgage Loan Act separately where the brokerage plans subordinate-lien activity.
evidence: Secondary license or registration evidence, products, effective dates and any exception.
counsel: Does the pilot include secondary mortgages, and which authority covers those transactions?

title: Individual origination authority
summary: Review each Michigan originator's individual authority and unique identifier for the activity and dates. The act identifies exceptions and temporary authority provisions.
evidence: Individual license, unique identifier, sponsorship and activity evidence. Test expired, absent and mismatched authority.
counsel: Confirm treatment of exemptions, temporary authority and independent contractors before enabling the eligibility check.

title: First mortgage company renewal
authority: Michigan DIFS first mortgage renewal guidance and MCL 445.1657(1)
summary: DIFS directs first mortgage company licensees and registrants to request renewal and pay through NMLS by December 15. The authority expires December 31 unless renewed.
evidence: Exact company license or registration, current renewal instructions, applicable surety bond, NMLS request and fee receipt, and renewed authority status.
counsel: Verify the applicable renewal-year instructions, financial responsibility evidence and treatment of pending or late renewal.

title: Secondary mortgage company renewal
authority: Michigan DIFS secondary mortgage renewal guidance and MCL 493.56a(1)
summary: DIFS directs secondary mortgage company licensees and registrants to request renewal and pay through NMLS by December 15. The authority expires December 31 unless renewed.
evidence: Exact company license or registration, current renewal instructions, applicable surety bond, NMLS request and fee receipt, and renewed authority status.
counsel: Confirm separate or coordinated renewal treatment when both authorities are held, current instructions and pending or late renewal consequences.

title: Individual MLO renewal and continuing education
summary: DIFS lists separate individual renewal requirements, including education before the request unless an exception applies. Its May 2026 FAQ and an older renewal checklist show different submission dates.
evidence: Individual authority and sponsor, current-year NMLS instructions, education or exception evidence, bond and renewed status.
counsel: Reconcile the current renewal-year instructions, older checklist, education exception and treatment of pending renewal before assigning individual dates.

title: Quarterly mortgage activity report
summary: DIFS directs covered licensees and registrants to submit mortgage activity through the quarterly NMLS Mortgage Call Report. FV7 workpapers can reconcile part of the saved quarter.
evidence: Exact entity/license and reporting state, prior balances, reconciled FV7 sections, documented no-activity treatment and filing receipt.
counsel: Confirm quarter applicability, state supplements, zero-activity handling and any period-specific relief.

title: NMLS Financial Condition
summary: DIFS describes annual calendar-year Financial Condition reporting for mortgage brokers and quarterly reporting for mortgage lenders and servicers.
evidence: Entity activity classification, reporting period, approved account mapping and financial workpaper.
counsel: Confirm which entity role governs when activities or licenses overlap and which FC sections apply.

title: Michigan fiscal-year financial statement
summary: DIFS describes a GAAP financial statement due within 90 days after the company fiscal year ends. Review this separately from NMLS Financial Condition.
evidence: Actual fiscal year-end, approved financial statement and submission evidence.
counsel: Confirm the entity's obligation, current delivery method, period and any exceptions.

title: First mortgage records and examination
authority: MCL 445.1671 and DIFS Mortgage Compliance FAQ
summary: DIFS distinguishes the broker-only first-mortgage file from a lender's transfer or assignment scenario. The statute separately addresses other business records.
evidence: Record class, closing or transfer basis, other applicable duties, holds and controlled examination export.
counsel: Confirm broker and lender record custody, federal overlays, overlapping state requirements and disposition triggers. No deletion timer should be inferred from one source.

title: Secondary mortgage records
authority: MCL 493.67–493.68 and DIFS Mortgage Compliance FAQ
summary: Review examination availability and the distinct retention triggers for general closed files, specified transferred copies, rejected applications and other business records under the Secondary Mortgage Loan Act.
evidence: Document type, role, retention trigger, custody and location, hold evidence, and exam delivery procedure.
counsel: Confirm applicable retention periods and overlaps before enabling a schedule.

title: Principal and branch registration
summary: Ohio's RMLA sets out registration for the principal and branch offices maintained for covered brokerage activity.
evidence: Entity registration, branch inventory, registered addresses and documented activity dates.
counsel: Confirm exemptions and how remote or shared offices fit the statute.

title: Loan broker and office licenses
authority: Indiana Secretary of State Loan Brokers
summary: The Securities Division distinguishes the loan broker, offices and associated managers and originators.
evidence: Broker authority, office and manager inventory, and NMLS evidence for the proposed activity.
counsel: Confirm whether the activity falls under the Securities Division loan broker regime or a different authorization and which locations qualify.

title: Residential mortgage brokerage authority
summary: Illinois's Residential Mortgage License Act addresses licensure for residential mortgage brokering and other specified activities.
evidence: Exact entity license, authorized activity, office basis and applicable exemption documentation.
counsel: Resolve entity and branch applicability, including any statutory exemption, before enabling workflow controls.

title: Mortgage broker authority
summary: Wisconsin DFI distinguishes mortgage banker and mortgage broker authority and directs company applications through NMLS.
evidence: Broker license and supported activities, office inventory and source dates.
counsel: Confirm covered activities, locations, exemptions and any overlapping banker license before activation.

title: First mortgage charges and processing fees
summary: The statute addresses reasonable and necessary actual expenses, loan processing fees, one-time payment of charges and written terms when a fee is assessed or accepted to guarantee an interest rate.
evidence: Fee schedule and actual expenses, payment history, responsible party and written rate-guarantee terms or extensions when applicable.
counsel: Which charges and guarantee duties apply to this entity and product? Confirm the interaction with TRID timing and federal compensation rules.

title: Michigan application booklet
summary: Michigan's Consumer Mortgage Protection Act addresses providing the special information booklet when a covered borrower applies. DIFS guidance discusses refinance applications, broker-provided evidence and channel-specific timing.
evidence: Covered transaction and responsible parties, state application event and channel, booklet version, provider, delivery time and supporting evidence.
counsel: Confirm coverage, the application trigger, which booklet and channel-specific timing apply, and what broker delivery evidence the lender must retain.

relatedSources.label: Michigan DIFS Consumer Mortgage Protection Act FAQ

title: Covered transaction service fees
summary: The Act addresses fees for products or services actually provided and accurate representation of third-party charges or payments on covered mortgage loans.
evidence: Covered transaction facts, actual service evidence, original invoice or third-party statement, disclosed and paid amounts, and any reconciliation.
counsel: Which transactions and brokerage activities are covered? Confirm how to document a disputed, partially provided or canceled service and the overlap with first-mortgage charges.

title: Application, representations and signed note
summary: Review borrower qualification and property-value representations, changes to application information and completed terms in the note when the borrower signs.
evidence: Source supporting the representation, original and revised application versions, who changed the facts and why, signed note and exception review.
counsel: Which controls are the brokerage's responsibility when the wholesale lender prepares the note? Confirm review of changes, audience and whether a representation could mislead.

title: Appraisal independence and payment terms
summary: The Act addresses payment conditioned on value or closing and improper influence over the appraiser's independent valuation.
evidence: Appraisal engagement and payment terms, communications, escalation reference, and wholesale lender or appraisal management company responsibility.
counsel: Confirm the brokerage and lender responsibilities and how the state provisions overlap with federal valuation-independence rules.

title: Financed single-premium credit insurance
summary: The Act prohibits a lender from financing single-premium credit life, credit disability or credit unemployment insurance as part of a covered mortgage loan.
evidence: Insurance type, premium structure, whether financed, lender evidence and any resolved exception.
counsel: Confirm the brokerage's review responsibility, treatment of premium arrangements and any independently applicable federal restriction.

title: Short-term payment schedule and bridge review
summary: The Act addresses full amortization through regular periodic payments on covered terms under five years and an exception for qualifying bridge maturities under one year.
evidence: Covered transaction facts, note and maturity, scheduled payments and remaining principal, and documented bridge purpose and intended occupancy when relevant.
counsel: Confirm the statutory coverage, term measurement, amortization calculation and exception basis before using an automated product check.

title: First mortgage advertising and advertised terms
summary: Covered licensees and registrants may not use misleading mortgage advertising. The statute also addresses intent to offer advertised loan terms to qualified applicants.
evidence: Final ad and audience, product and terms substantiation, qualification criteria, and approval evidence before publication.
counsel: Confirm which campaigns, affiliates and products fall within this section and which additional state and federal disclosures or restrictions apply.

title: Secondary mortgage advertising and advertised terms
summary: Review secondary mortgage advertising for the act's misrepresentation standard and substantiate the terms available to applicants who meet the documented qualifications.
evidence: Exact creative and audience, secondary mortgage authority, qualification criteria, contemporaneous product terms and any correction evidence.
counsel: Confirm secondary mortgage scope, treatment of mixed campaigns and how to evaluate the act's mental-state standard.

title: Originator advertising and visible identifier
authority: MCL 493.165(c), MCL 493.171 and DIFS originator FAQ
summary: Review the originator's advertising claims and whether each applicable individual's identifier is clear on the final creative. DIFS separately recommends showing the sponsoring mortgage company's identifier.
evidence: Exact creative, verified and displayed originator identifiers, visibility, company and sponsorship evidence, and media or placement.
counsel: Confirm which originators and materials are covered, identifier prominence for each channel, and any separate company identification obligation.

title: Indiana loan broker agreement and borrower copy
authority: Ind. Code §23-2.5-8-1 and Indiana Securities Division agreement form
summary: The Securities Division publishes a loan broker agreement form. The state mortgage task force identifies the borrower copy and signed agreement as examination concerns.
evidence: Current approved agreement, signed copy, borrower delivery evidence and transaction role.
counsel: Confirm the operative form, signatures, delivery timing, applicable fees and the entities or activities subject to the agreement.

relatedSources.label: Indiana Mortgage Lending and Fraud Prevention Task Force report

title: Reports of condition and consummated loan coverage
summary: The statute requires NMLS reports from listed registrants, licensees and valid exemption-letter holders. It also specifies consummated and serviced loans that registrants and exemption-letter holders must include.
evidence: Entity status, period, Ohio activity reconciliation, required report fields and submission receipt.
counsel: Confirm the reporting party, any supplementary schedules, the applicable FV7 calendar and zero-activity treatment.

title: NMLS reports in lieu of listed activity reports
authority: Illinois IDFPR Mortgage Brokers and Bankers Forms
summary: IDFPR accepts timely and accurate NMLS Mortgage Call Reports in place of its listed annual mortgage, brokerage, servicing and purchasing activity reports.
evidence: License scope, accepted NMLS submission and timeliness, reconciliation by activity, and an inventory of separate state filings.
counsel: Confirm treatment of late or corrected filings and which separate financial, fair lending, database or servicing obligations apply to the entity.

title: Annual CPA financial statements
authority: Wis. Stat. §224.74(1)(b), (bm) and DFI Mortgage Banking FAQ
summary: DFI directs mortgage brokers to submit reviewed and mortgage bankers to submit audited financial statements via NMLS within six months of fiscal year end.
evidence: Exact license type, fiscal year end, CPA statement, submission receipt and any regulator correspondence.
counsel: Confirm the statement basis for a dual licensee, the deadline in edge cases and how to track this separately from current FV7 Financial Condition.

title: Borrower instructions and broker duties
summary: The section addresses safeguarding buyer funds, lawful instructions, care, fair dealing and reasonable efforts to seek advantageous terms from regular lender relationships. Division (A) excludes wholesale lenders.
evidence: Borrower instructions, options reviewed with regular lenders, rationale, handled-funds reconciliation and party roles.
counsel: Confirm the entity's role, any wholesale-lender exclusion and what comparison evidence demonstrates reasonable efforts.

title: Advertising name and unique identifier
summary: Mortgage service advertisements across listed media, including internet sites, must disclose the covered registrant's or originator's business name and unique identifier.
evidence: Final copy or recording by channel, applicable names and identifiers, approval, publication date and archive reference.
counsel: Confirm which identifiers apply to company, originator and jointly branded advertising and how the rule's federal cross-reference applies.

title: Borrower file and examination retention
summary: The rule describes a searchable obtained-loan spreadsheet, borrower files for applications and advertising files. Its four-year period starts on closing, withdrawal or denial for loan records and dissemination for advertising.
evidence: Closed and unclosed application files, published ad archive, disclosure versions, searchable loan register, event dates and retrieval evidence.
counsel: Confirm entity coverage, storage and indexing controls, non-erasable electronic retention and the appropriate trigger for unresolved files.

title: Commissioner-required loan broker reports of condition
summary: The statute provides for loan broker reports of condition when required by the commissioner, with the form and content the commissioner requires and submission to the commissioner and NMLS.
evidence: Applicable commissioner instruction, reporting period, required fields, entity and license, NMLS and any separate delivery receipts.
counsel: Confirm how the Division currently implements the statute, including whether NMLS satisfies both routes, applicable periods, and no-activity and amendment treatment.

title: Preclosing fees and unspent deposit review
authority: Indiana Securities Division Loan Broker Agreement and 710 IAC 1-22-6
summary: The Division's agreement addresses bona fide third-party fees before closing, return of unspent deposits on cancellation, and source of broker compensation.
evidence: Signed agreement, fee category, collection time and amount, invoices, unspent deposit reconciliation, refund receipt and payer evidence.
counsel: Confirm permissible fees and refund triggers, the role of the collecting party and overlap with the federal fee and compensation rules.

title: Solicitation materials in examination files
authority: Ind. Code §23-2.5-8-5(4) and Securities Division documents request
summary: The Division's examination request includes advertising and marketing materials across media, including internet and social ads. The statute lists solicitation samples and distribution criteria for certain internet communications.
evidence: Published material, dates, channels, recipient counts where relevant, script or final rendition and examination archive.
counsel: Confirm when the statutory sample and internet distribution provisions apply, and follow the exact examination notice for the requested scope.

relatedSources.label: Indiana Securities Division documents and records request

title: Loan broker application files and searchable examination report
summary: The statute addresses applicant and prospective-applicant files, a searchable report including pending and unclosed loans, and two-year office retention. It provides separate access options for out-of-state offices.
evidence: Signed agreements and disclosures, creditor and originator, receipts and disbursements, disposition, search by borrower last name, and retention and retrieval evidence.
counsel: Confirm office and electronic retention, the report population for inquiries and applications, and different rules for a DFI-regulated entity.

relatedSources.label: Indiana loan broker records required by statute
Indiana Securities Division documents and records request

title: Signed loan brokerage agreement and borrower copy
summary: Covered loan brokerage requires a signed written agreement before the earlier of signing the completed application or giving consideration. The agreement incorporates the brokerage disclosure and the executed copy goes to the customer.
evidence: Approved agreement and incorporated disclosure, borrower and licensee signatures, application signature and consideration timestamps, and borrower copy evidence.
counsel: Confirm covered role, treatment of electronic signatures, exact copy and disclosure timing, and any additional state or federal disclosure requirements.

title: Mortgage advertising license and identifiers
authority: 205 ILCS 635/3-3 and 38 Ill. Adm. Code Subpart H
summary: The Act and rules address licensed or exempt advertising, misleading claims and conditions for using the licensee's NMLS identifier, including mixed-activity material.
evidence: Final advertisement, product and audience, authority and identifiers, approval and evidence supporting advertised claims.
counsel: Confirm identification, prominence and other content rules for the channels and products in scope, including joint or mixed-activity advertising.

title: Broker or origination loan log
summary: The broker or origination log covers applications received with identifiers, status and closing details. The rule separately addresses reverse mortgages and shared appreciation agreements.
evidence: Application population and order, field mapping, closed and unclosed status evidence, and product-specific log or documented exclusion.
counsel: Confirm which products are in scope and how to document unavailable fields and retain the log securely for examination.

title: Broker records retention and digital reproduction
summary: For brokerage or origination records the rule provides a 36-month period from closing or other termination of the loan process and conditions for digital retention and paper conversion.
evidence: Closing or termination date, paper conversion process and original disposition, retained versions and legible reproduction.
counsel: Confirm the controlling retention trigger, examination format and any overlapping requirements or hold extending the minimum.

title: Broker agreement and separate consumer disclosure
summary: DFI provides separate closed-end TRID, other closed-end and open-end agreements and the MB600 consumer disclosure.
evidence: Applicable agreement and MB600 version, broker role, signatures, compensation terms and evidence of delivery relative to the applicable trigger.
counsel: Confirm approved form selection, the timing of the separate disclosure and agreement, and responsibilities for companion federal disclosures.

title: Identifier on applications, solicitations and advertising
summary: The statute addresses clear placement of identifiers on applications and solicitations, including websites, business cards and email signatures. It also addresses misleading affiliation claims.
evidence: Final communication or application, applicable identifier, channel, copy approval and substantiation for any affiliation claim.
counsel: Confirm which entity and individual identifiers are required by channel, and review co-branded materials and government-related representations.

title: Application records, fee disposition and retention
summary: The statute addresses application and fee records and a 36-month retention period beginning at closing or, for unclosed loans, application. It separately addresses banker-serviced loans.
evidence: Fee ledger and disposition, application outcome and reason, applicable file documents, retention event, approved location and retrieval evidence.
counsel: Confirm covered file contents, location and access, treatment of applications that never close and any longer federal or examination retention obligation.

title: Residential mortgage originator company authority
summary: Minnesota addresses residential mortgage originator licensing and specified exemptions in Chapter 58.
evidence: Exact company authority and activity, exemption basis where relevant, and separately verified individual authority.
counsel: Confirm the company classification, exceptions and applicability to the proposed office, product and borrower scope.

title: Originator and servicer reports of condition
summary: The statute requires residential mortgage originators and servicers to submit reports of condition in the form required by NMLS.
evidence: Company role, license, reporting period, reconciled report and receipt.
counsel: Confirm entity applicability, the current FV7 sections, any supplementary filings and the no-activity basis.

title: Mortgage banker or broker company authority
summary: The statute addresses licensure for acting as or using the title of a mortgage banker, broker or closing agent in Iowa.
evidence: License class and activity, license dates, office evidence and any exemption basis.
counsel: Confirm whether proposed brokering, funding or closing duties fall under separate authority or any exception.

title: Mortgage call reports under the October 2026 rule
authority: Iowa Admin. Code 187–18.10 and Iowa Code §535B.18
summary: Rule 187–18.10 requires licensed mortgage bankers and brokers to submit reports under §535B.18 and addresses late fees after the NMLS-established due date. The published rule took effect October 21, 2026.
evidence: License, relevant reporting period and source version, NMLS due date and receipt.
counsel: Confirm which periods use this rule, applicable FV7 sections and any additional or no-activity filing treatment.

title: Residential mortgage loan broker company authority
summary: The statute requires residential mortgage loan broker authority for specified brokering, funding, servicing or purchasing activities, subject to exceptions.
evidence: Company license, role and activities, office facts, individual authority and exemption evidence where relevant.
counsel: Confirm authorized activities, office requirements and exemptions for this entity and products.

title: Annual mortgage activity report
summary: The statute sets March 1 for covered brokers' annual activity reports and permits the director to accept a report deemed equivalent.
evidence: Prior calendar-year activity, annual report and receipt, or documented regulator acceptance of the proposed substitute.
counsel: Confirm current filing instructions, which exemptions apply and whether any specific NMLS or other filing is accepted as equivalent for this scope.

title: Mortgage banker authority for covered brokerage
summary: The statute addresses authority to act as a mortgage banker, including licensing and other specified pathways.
evidence: Entity activity, license or registration evidence, branch and individual authority, and any exemption basis.
counsel: Confirm which activity definitions and licensing pathways apply to the proposed brokerage.

title: Mortgage reports of condition
summary: The statute requires NMLS reports of condition for licensed mortgage bankers, registrants and installment loan companies, in the form the department requires.
evidence: Exact license or registration, relevant period, reconciled report, reporting calendar and submission receipt.
counsel: Confirm current dates and form requirements under FV7, including whether older department orders affect the applicable period.

title: Mortgage brokerage company authority
authority: SDCL §54-14-13 and Division of Banking Mortgage Licenses
summary: The statute addresses authority for covered mortgage activity involving South Dakota property. The division distinguishes mortgage brokerages that place loans for a fee without servicing from lenders and servicers.
evidence: Property jurisdiction, company authority, authorized activities and individual authority, with exemption evidence where relevant.
counsel: Confirm correct license classification, exceptions, and location and sponsorship requirements.

relatedSources.label: South Dakota Division of Banking license types

title: Mortgage brokerage reports of condition
summary: The statute identifies mortgage lenders, mortgage brokerages, mortgage brokers and mortgage loan originators for NMLS reports of condition.
evidence: Company license class, applicable reporting period, reconciled report and submission evidence.
counsel: Confirm current state instructions and FV7 sections, deadlines, supplements and no-activity treatment.

title: Residential mortgage lender license for covered arranging
summary: North Dakota's residential mortgage lender chapter includes covered arranging and solicitation. The company licensing trigger refers to borrower residence.
evidence: Borrower residence and property location, exact company and branch authority, activity and any exception.
counsel: Confirm company authority under Chapter 13-12 for residential activity, distinct money-broker rules where relevant and the separate individual MLO nexus.

title: Residential mortgage lender call reports
summary: The residential mortgage lender chapter requires its licensees to submit reports of condition to NMLS.
evidence: Chapter 13-12 license, covered activity, reporting period, current report and receipt.
counsel: Confirm current FV7 coverage, any state supplemental fields and zero-activity handling for the specific entity.

title: Mortgage company license and remote activity
summary: The statute addresses mortgage company licensure, specified exemptions, remote mortgage business conditions and individual loan originator registration.
evidence: Company and branch authority, proposed remote activity facts, individual registrations and any exemption basis.
counsel: Confirm the company and individual authority, branch versus remote status and the scope of the activities.

title: Annual report and Kansas supplemental form
summary: OSBC says the MCR plus the State Specific Supplemental Form satisfies annual reporting and identifies processing and underwriting lines SF600 through SF660 for applicable Kansas transactions.
evidence: Kansas activity, current MCR and supplemental form, processing and underwriting reconciliation and submission receipt.
counsel: Confirm which activities belong on the supplemental form, FV7 field treatment, no-activity handling and any separate surrender report.

title: Refinance tangible net benefit evidence
summary: The churning provision addresses reasonable, tangible net benefit. It calls for written evidence of circumstances at application and borrower signature before closing to demonstrate the benefit.
evidence: Existing and proposed terms, transaction costs, borrower circumstances at application, benefit rationale and signature date.
counsel: Confirm covered refinance scenarios, exceptions, borrower signatures and the state and federal benefit tests that apply.

title: Mortgage advertising claims and terms
summary: The standards address false, misleading or deceptive mortgage marketing and representations across channels.
evidence: Final copy, terms and product substantiation, audience, dissemination dates and review record.
counsel: Confirm applicable channel rules and which entity or exempt person is responsible for jointly distributed material.

title: Residential mortgage business records
summary: The statute calls for 60 months of business records for a licensee or exempt person, including communications, incomplete documentation and ads for covered activity.
evidence: Application status and file records, email and applicable recordings, advertisements, retention policy and retrieval rehearsal.
counsel: Confirm applicable retention start events, recording and consent obligations, and the scope for exempt persons.

title: Prohibited acts and loan evidence
summary: Chapter 535B applies the prohibited acts in §535D.17 to licensees. Review mortgage representations, required disclosures and independent valuation controls against the incorporated provision.
evidence: Versioned disclosures, representations and support, valuation communications and escalation evidence.
counsel: Confirm how the incorporated prohibitions apply to the brokerage, the individual originator and third-party communications.

title: Available terms and licensee identifier in advertising
summary: From the October 2026 rule transition, review availability of advertised products and terms, material restrictions, clarity and the licensee's NMLS identifier.
evidence: Published sample by channel, available product and terms at publication, limitations, NMLS identifier and approval.
counsel: Confirm applicability for advertisements spanning the transition and how the federal advertising provisions apply.

title: Mortgage broker application index, log and files
summary: The rule addresses the broker's index, log and files and 36-month retention from the final transaction. It separately defines when information becomes an application for the state log.
evidence: Indexed files including unclosed dispositions, evidence of receipt of the name and Social Security number without copying the number into review notes, last transaction, and secure retrieval.
counsel: Confirm the log's application trigger separately from TRID, final transaction dates for each disposition and responsibilities after surrender.

title: Mortgage banker fiscal-year audited statements
summary: Section 535B.10(1) addresses filing audited statements by a mortgage banker licensee within 120 days of fiscal year end. The October rule addresses late filing.
evidence: Banker license basis, fiscal year end, independent audit, current filing route and regulator receipt.
counsel: Confirm the actual license category and separate state submission basis. Resolve any distinct requirement for a broker-only entity.

title: Electronic origination data capability
summary: The rule addresses the capability to provide electronic origination characteristics within 30 days of quarter end, another interval set by the administrator, or examination notice. Broker access to particular fields is qualified.
evidence: Current administrator format and interval, field-by-field access and availability, export rehearsal and applicable request evidence.
counsel: Confirm the current field specification given the printed 18.16(11) cross-reference, whether a file must be delivered, and handling of fields the broker neither prepares nor knows and cannot reasonably access.

title: Brokerage disclosure statement and fee agreement
summary: The statement and agreement address whether the broker makes loans, whether another party may provide funds and affect availability, and the amounts and sources of fees and compensation.
evidence: Exact agreement version, role and funding disclosure, compensation sources and amounts, actual fee reconciliation and borrower evidence.
counsel: Confirm delivery and acceptance evidence, the effect of any variance from disclosed fees, and federal compensation overlap.

title: Mortgage advertising and license representations
summary: The section addresses advertising rulemaking for covered mortgage loans and limits representations of regulation or oversight.
evidence: Published ad, marketed products, evidence for representations and approved description of license or oversight.
counsel: Confirm applicable rules for the channels, required license information and wording for any claimed government affiliation.

title: Credit application record retention
summary: The licensing duties include keeping the written records required under ECOA and other director-required information for 36 months.
evidence: Applicable application and decision evidence, completeness and disposition dates, retention policy and examination retrieval.
counsel: Confirm the state retention trigger and record set, applicable federal overlays and any longer examination or hold requirement.

title: Refinance net tangible benefit worksheet
summary: The statute calls for disclosure of whether a refinance provides a net tangible benefit, using the director's worksheet or a prescribed substantially similar form.
evidence: Existing and proposed terms, fees, documented benefit assessment, worksheet version and borrower delivery proof.
counsel: Confirm applicability, the operative form, timing and how the licensee documents cases with no identified benefit.

relatedSources.label: Nebraska Department of Banking and Finance prescribed form, revised October 15, 2026

title: Unique identifier on applications and advertisements
summary: The statute addresses clear display of the unique identifier on application forms, solicitations and ads, including business cards and websites.
evidence: Final application form and channel examples, company and originator identifiers, approvals and archive references.
counsel: Confirm which licensee's identifier belongs on each channel and any additional director-designated documents.

title: Mortgage application and loan retention
summary: The mortgage banker duty covers loan and application documents for five years after funding, denial or withdrawal.
evidence: Closed and unclosed records, authoritative disposition dates, disclosure versions, archive references and retrieval checks.
counsel: Confirm the role, treatment of unresolved dispositions and longer overlapping requirements.

title: Appraisal independence and fee conditions
summary: The chapter addresses improper influence on valuation and distinguishes specified actions that do not constitute improper influence.
evidence: Engagement and payment terms, communications, request purpose, independent review and escalation evidence.
counsel: Confirm the covered party's interest, permitted requests, and overlap with federal valuation independence.

title: Advertising or holding out under mortgage authority
summary: The chapter addresses advertising or holding out as a mortgage lender, broker, brokerage or originator without required authority.
evidence: Final claims, covered properties, license and role on publication date, publication record and approval.
counsel: Confirm scope for digital, multistate and joint campaigns, applicable exemptions and any separate identifier and content rules.

title: Mortgage broker records for examination
summary: The statute subjects licensees and registrants to examinations. The Division directs mortgage brokers to Chapter 20:07:19 for operative records and exam rules.
evidence: License and role, file inventory, financial records, retention and retrieval procedure, examination notice and produced records.
counsel: Confirm the applicable sections, record categories, duration and scope of the current examination request.

title: Advance expense deposits and rate-lock fee review
summary: The statute addresses advance fees, licensed advance expense deposits for specified independent appraisal or credit report costs, refund or credit of excess, and rate-lock fees.
evidence: Authority, fee category and collection date, third-party cost estimate and invoice, excess reconciliation, refund or credit and lock terms.
counsel: Confirm covered charges and parties, product and license exemptions, and interaction with federal fee timing.

title: Availability of advertised financing terms
summary: The statute addresses whether stated terms were actually available when marketed and prohibits deceptive representations about loan terms.
evidence: Final ad, actual pricing and product availability, distribution dates, restrictions and review evidence.
counsel: Confirm which marketing and loan discussions are covered and the appropriate evidence for a limited offer.

title: Loan and collections retention from last entry
summary: The section addresses records of collected sums and completed loans for six years from the last entry. It permits electronic records subject to reproduction and separately addresses records custody after cessation.
evidence: Transaction ledger and last entry, completed loan evidence, retrieval test and any post-cessation custody notice.
counsel: Confirm which entries start the period and any separate duties for unclosed files, other roles and loan records.

title: Consumer notice before the earliest applicable event
authority: K.S.A. 9-2208(b) and K.A.R. 17-24-1 as amended July 24, 2026
summary: Give a written notice before the earliest applicable contract, compensation or promise of compensation, or servicing-transfer deadline. The July 2026 rule specifies the notice date, company name and address, and prescribed statement in at least 10-point boldface.
evidence: Notice edition and format, evidence of when it was provided to each consumer, contract and compensation or promise dates, and any servicing transfer date.
counsel: Confirm the notice and delivery evidence, the operative requirements for historical transactions, and the earliest applicable event for the exact brokerage role.

relatedSources.label: Kansas OSBC current notice contents rule

title: Kansas solicitation name, identifier and archive
summary: The section addresses licensed name and identifier on solicitations and published ads directed at Kansas residents, a 36-month archive and misleading content restrictions.
evidence: Final communication, targeting and audience, legal or registered name, identifier, publication date and archive reference.
counsel: Confirm the treatment of business cards, promotional items, co-branded materials and the applicable archive trigger.

title: Brokered mortgage file retention
summary: For mortgages the licensee does not close in its own name, the rule addresses applicable file records retained for at least 36 months from closing or from application if the loan does not close.
evidence: Closing or application date, borrower notice and applicable state and federal evidence, retained file and retrieval rehearsal.
counsel: Confirm the operative version by file date, record contents and any longer regulator or federal requirement.

title: Mortgage broker authority
summary: Pennsylvania's Mortgage Licensing Act identifies separate broker, lender, correspondent and originator licensing categories for covered mortgage business.
evidence: Exact company license class, activity, office basis and any exception evidence.
counsel: Confirm whether planned first and secondary business, staffing and offices fall within the company's license or an exception.

title: Periodic first and secondary mortgage reporting
summary: Pennsylvania requires listed licensees including mortgage brokers to file periodic reports as the department determines, through the department or NMLS.
evidence: License class, reporting period, first and secondary mortgage reconciliations, filing instructions and receipt.
counsel: Confirm the current form, cadence, route and state additions, including any treatment for periods without activity.

title: Mortgage broker registration
summary: New York distinguishes registration for covered solicitation, processing, placement or negotiation of mortgage loans from mortgage banker licensing.
evidence: Company registration, role and product evidence, activity dates, office scope and any exception basis.

title: Third-party fee trust and examination records
summary: Oklahoma requires a trust account for qualifying third-party funds and current, accessible records for at least three years after the effective period to which the records relate.
evidence: Receipts, trust deposit and disbursement dates, reconciled ledger and bank evidence, records location and exam production.
counsel: Confirm who holds the funds, what starts retention and the time and method for examiner access.

title: Written deposit disposition and trust funds
summary: An application deposit required by the licensee calls for a written agreement on its disposition whether or not the loan is consummated. The rule addresses trust handling for covered funds.
evidence: Written agreement, receipt and trust ledger, disbursement or refund and file disposition.
counsel: Confirm covered funds, refund and reconciliation rules, and current federal limits on advance collection.

title: Originator identifier on solicitations and ads
summary: The rule requires the originator unique identifier on residential applications, solicitations and advertisements, including business cards and websites.
evidence: Published samples and application forms, originator ID and sponsorship, placement and approvals.
counsel: Confirm applicable company and individual identifiers and additional rules by medium.

title: Loan file, compensation and funded journal records
summary: The rule lists records for examination, including disclosures, fee and compensation evidence, account journals and the funded loan journal. It covers electronic records.
evidence: File inventory and disposition, dated disclosures, compensation and funded journal references, and retrieval sample.
counsel: Confirm current equivalents for older named forms, file categories for unclosed loans, retention and exam format.

title: Borrower benefit and historical disclosure form
authority: C.R.S. §12-10-710; repeal of 4 CCR 725-3 Rules 5.7 and 5.8
summary: The statute addresses reasonable inquiry and borrower benefit. The Board repealed the prescribed form rules effective September 30, 2025 and approved related cleanup effective March 17, 2026.
evidence: Transaction date, terms, costs, borrower circumstances and inquiry, benefit rationale, and historical form where applicable.
counsel: Confirm applicable statutory duties and product scope, date-specific forms and the evidence supporting current decisions.

title: Mortgage advertising identity and available terms
summary: The Board's advertising rules address actually available products and material limitations, conspicuous responsible-party and company information, exceptions and an advertising archive.
evidence: Dated published creative, terms availability, material limits, responsible-party identity and retention sample.
counsel: Confirm the operative version, channel exceptions and required identifiers and retention.

title: Loan origination records for Board investigations
summary: The Board's investigation procedure addresses responsive records such as applications, disclosures and supporting transaction documentation, and provides for a timely written request for extension.
evidence: Board notice, due date and extension evidence, loan file and disclosure records, and scoped production receipt.
counsel: Confirm operative rule, records and retention by role and file disposition, and production instructions.

title: Written agreement for covered loan funds or documents
summary: For covered applications of $200,000 or less, the statute limits acceptance of funds or documents and requires a signed agreement with disposition, term and estimated cost information. It also addresses specified fees and segregation.
evidence: Loan amount, signed agreement and estimated costs, items received, fee purpose, ledger and return or disposition evidence.
counsel: Confirm current threshold, scope and timing for each item and any federal collection restrictions.

title: Licensed name and number on advertising and solicitation
summary: Arizona addresses use of the licensed or filed name and license number in mortgage advertising and solicitation. It describes certain channel and promotional-item exclusions.
evidence: Published item and channel, approved name and license number, market and advertised rate or term.
counsel: Confirm channel and content exceptions and any separate originator identifier duty.

title: Closed loan retention and response to regulator demand
summary: The statute requires original or legible records of mortgage transactions for at least five years after closing and production in Arizona within three business days after demand.
evidence: Closing and demand dates, records location and contents, production dates and receipt.
counsel: Confirm unclosed-file retention, offsite requirements and longer applicable obligations.

title: Signed statement of fee and deposit refund conditions
summary: Utah limits charges and requires a written statement signed by the applicant describing whether the fee or deposit is refundable and the conditions for refund.
evidence: Dated signed statement, fee or deposit and timing, refund basis and disposition.
counsel: Confirm covered charges, cancellation and fee exceptions, form and federal collection limits.

title: First-lien valuation delivery and waiver evidence
summary: Utah specifies delivery timing for each appraisal or written valuation in covered first-lien dwelling transactions, with limited waivers and a separate delivery rule when a waived transaction does not complete.
evidence: Valuation versions, completion and delivery dates, proposed settlement, waiver and known noncompletion date.
counsel: Confirm responsible party, applicable business-day definition and federal overlap, waiver limits and triggers.

title: False and misleading mortgage advertising
summary: Utah prohibits false or misleading mortgage advertising and addresses representations by persons exempt under the specified provision.
evidence: Published creative and channel, claims support, responsible party and authority, and approval.
counsel: Confirm company and originator identity and applicable advertising rules by channel.

title: Safeguarded mortgage files and latest-event retention
summary: Utah requires four years of retention from the latest applicable final entry, servicing event, or closing for a nonserviced loan. Required records must be made available for inspection.
evidence: File records, dated final entry and closing or servicing events, evidence of custody and inspection retrieval.
counsel: Confirm trigger treatment for unclosed files, applicable record classes and longer obligations.

title: Itemized mortgage company fee disclosure
summary: Nevada requires a disclosure for covered real-property-secured loans listing fees earned by the company in specific dollar amounts, the responsible party and probable impact.
evidence: Itemized company fees and payors, impact explanation, disclosure version and delivery, and closing reconciliation.
counsel: Confirm covered fees and parties, MLD Form 201 applicability, timing and federal overlap.

title: Advertising identity and submission for newer licensees
authority: NRS 645B.189; NAC 645B.240 as amended by R070-23
summary: The adopted regulation addresses name, contact and license or identifier information and joint ads. MLD also directs companies licensed for less than 12 months to submit advertising for review.
evidence: Dated creative and channels, identifiers and names, license dates, submission and approval and any cost allocation.
counsel: Confirm scope and timing of submission or approval, medium exceptions, and whether other lender names require consent.

title: Completed and unclosed transaction records
summary: Nevada distinguishes completed records kept for at least four years after the last related activity from denied or withdrawn applications kept for at least one year or as required under federal law.
evidence: Disposition, last related activity, file inventory, office and electronic access, and exam retrieval.
counsel: Confirm trigger and retention by record category, longer federal requirements and remote records access.

title: DRE broker or corporation endorsement
authority: California DRE mortgage loan originator endorsement guidance
summary: DRE describes endorsements for covered activity under an underlying real estate license, including company and designated broker-officer requirements for corporations.
evidence: DRE broker or corporate license, company and individual endorsements, sponsorship, role and approved offices.
counsel: Confirm the DRE authority and activity scope, including when a DFPI authority applies instead or in addition.

title: California Financing Law broker authority
authority: California Financial Code §22000 et seq. and DFPI guidance
summary: DFPI explains that a California Financing Law broker license authorizes arranging loans with licensed finance lenders.
evidence: Exact CFL authority, counterparties and their license status, activity and individual authority.
counsel: Confirm counterparty eligibility, any exemptions and overlap with the DRE and CRMLA licensing paths.

title: DFPI residential mortgage lender or servicer authority
authority: Cal. Fin. Code §50000 et seq. and DFPI CRMLA guidance
summary: DFPI distinguishes lender, servicer and combined CRMLA authority and describes brokerage services permitted for licensed CRMLA lenders.
evidence: Exact company and branch authority, lending or servicing activity, eligible counterparties and individual licenses.
counsel: Confirm the exact authorization and exemption basis, branch and sponsor facts, and when limited brokerage activity is covered.

title: DRE Business Activity Report
authority: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §10166.07 and DRE RE 881 instructions
summary: DRE instructions describe electronic filing within 90 days after fiscal year end and instruct entering zero for items with no activity.
evidence: Applicable DRE authority and period, fiscal year end, activity or supported zero entries, filing and receipt.
counsel: Confirm the statutory trigger, any other mortgage reports, and applicability for licensees with an inactive period.

title: DFPI California Financing Law annual report
authority: Cal. Fin. Code §22159 and DFPI licensee instructions
summary: DFPI identifies a March 15 annual report for CFL licensees even when no business was conducted under the license.
evidence: CFL license, report-year instructions, reconciled activity or no-activity basis and submission receipt.
counsel: Confirm exact report-year deadline, delivery and scope when the company holds multiple California authorities.

title: DFPI California Financing Law quarterly residential mortgage activity
authority: Cal. Fin. Code §22159(c)–(d), 10 CCR §1430.5(b) and NMLS FV7 instructions
summary: DFPI directs covered residential mortgage lenders and brokers under the California Financing Law to file the NMLS Mortgage Call Report. The NMLS FV7 loan activity component is due within 45 days after the calendar quarter.
evidence: CFL authority, residential scope, reconciled quarterly activity or zero-activity basis, filing version and NMLS receipt.
counsel: Confirm coverage for the license and activities, when a commercial-only entity may disregard a reminder, whether a receipt supports another California authority, and the separate Financial Condition component.

relatedSources.label: NMLS FV7 submission dates and components

title: DFPI California Financing Law annual assessment
authority: Cal. Fin. Code §22107 and DFPI licensee instructions
summary: DFPI describes annual assessment notice by September 30 and payment by October 31. Review the actual assessment for each licensed location.
evidence: Assessment notice and invoice year, license and licensed locations, amount due, payment and DFPI receipt or reconciliation.
counsel: Confirm the assessed entity, payment deadline and handling of a missing or disputed notice, location changes or license status issues.

title: DFPI residential mortgage lender or servicer annual report
authority: Cal. Fin. Code §50307 and DFPI CRMLA annual report instructions
summary: DFPI requires CRMLA licensees to submit the prior calendar year's annual report through its self-service portal by March 1.
evidence: CRMLA authority, report-year schedules, reconciled loan and servicing data, authorized attestation and portal receipt.
counsel: Confirm the report-year instructions, reportable population, no-activity schedules and authorized attestation.

title: Holden Act residential mortgage loan report or response
authority: DFPI Residential Mortgage Loan Report guidance
summary: DFPI identifies March 31 for the prior-year report and describes circumstances in which the licensee provides a signed response explaining why it is not filing loan data.
evidence: License and first year of authority, covered loan analysis, applicable HMDA submission or no-activity basis, current DFPI form and transmission evidence.
counsel: Confirm the current report-year form and route, HMDA treatment, first-year and no-activity treatment, and whether the signed response is required.

title: DFPI residential mortgage quarterly call report
summary: DFPI directs CRMLA licensees to file the quarterly Mortgage Call Report through NMLS within 45 days after quarter end.
evidence: Company and license scope, current NMLS components, quarterly reconciliation and filing receipt.
counsel: Confirm reporting components, which authorities share the same NMLS submission, and treatment of inactivity.

title: CRMLA audited financial statements and supplements
authority: Cal. Fin. Code §50200, 10 CCR §1950.200 and DFPI CRMLA guidance
summary: DFPI directs CRMLA licensees to post audited financial statements in NMLS within 105 days after fiscal year end and identifies additional CPA or trust reconciliation evidence.
evidence: Actual fiscal year end, signed CPA audit, tangible net worth evidence, applicable supplementary reports and NMLS upload receipt.
counsel: Confirm the fiscal basis, annual audit coverage and supplementary documents or substitutions applicable to origination and servicing.

title: Mortgage broker company authority
authority: ORS 86A and Oregon DFR licensing guidance
summary: DFR directs covered mortgage bankers and brokers to apply through NMLS and describes company requirements.
evidence: License and role, locations, originators, handling of client funds and exemption evidence.
counsel: Confirm company and office scope, when the trust account provisions apply and any exception.

title: Oregon annual mortgage business report
summary: The statute describes an annual mortgage banker or broker report by May 1 or another date set by rule.
evidence: License, operative calendar, director-prescribed form, applicable activity and submission evidence.
counsel: Confirm any current alternative date or accepted NMLS substitute and the treatment of no activity.

title: Mortgage broker company authority
summary: DFI administers the Washington mortgage broker license and publishes separate broker resources for license applications, reports and examinations.
evidence: Company and location authority, individual licenses, business activities and any applicable exemption evidence.
counsel: Confirm broker versus consumer loan company authority and any branch or individual requirements.

title: Washington mortgage broker call reports
authority: Washington DFI Mortgage Call Reports and FV7 interim guidance
summary: DFI directs broker companies to file NMLS call reports. Its Q1 2026 FV7 interim guidance was specific to that filing period.
evidence: Company license, applicable period and rule, reconciled NMLS activity and receipt.
counsel: Confirm the operative FV7 calendar, Financial Condition classification and whether relief applies to the specific period.

title: Broker records and examination evidence
authority: Washington DFI Mortgage Broker Examinations guidance
summary: DFI describes retaining mortgage broker loan, advertising and financial records for at least three years from last use or activity.
evidence: Record classes, last use or activity, access controls, holds and examination export.
counsel: Confirm retention triggers and overlapping duties before enabling any disposition schedule.

title: Mortgage broker or mortgage lender authority
authority: Idaho Code §26-31-206 and Department of Finance
summary: Idaho Department of Finance regulates mortgage brokering, lending and other specified activities under the Idaho Residential Mortgage Practices Act.
evidence: Company and office authority, activity and individual licenses, and exemption evidence.
counsel: Confirm correct role and licensing scope for brokerage, modifications and independent processing.

title: Mortgage advertising and solicitation practices
summary: Idaho's mortgage practices rules address deceptive advertising, including misleading terms or claims of affiliation with a mortgage holder or agency.
evidence: Approved copy, substantiation, audience, sender and distribution evidence.
counsel: Confirm media and activity scope, required identifiers and overlap with other state and federal marketing requirements.

title: Montana mortgage broker company authority
authority: Montana Mortgage Act and state license guide
summary: Montana publishes a mortgage broker license guide with authorized activities, separate from lender and servicer categories.
evidence: Company and branch authority, activities, sponsored individuals and any exemption evidence.
counsel: Confirm which activities are covered and which require lender, servicer or other authority.

title: Montana broker quarterly mortgage call reports
authority: Montana Banking and Financial Institutions Division broker guide
summary: Montana's broker guide describes quarterly call reports and a Financial Condition component. The guide uses older form and fiscal-year terminology.
evidence: Exact license, applicable period and current FV7 instructions, reconciled figures and receipt.
counsel: Resolve the current Financial Condition basis, filing dates and no-activity treatment for the entity.

title: Mortgage broker or lender company authority
authority: Wyo. Stat. §40-23-104 and Division of Banking
summary: Wyoming distinguishes mortgage broker and lender company licenses and exempt registrations in its licensing and renewal guidance.
evidence: Company authority and role, location and individual licenses, and documented exception.
counsel: Confirm when each license or registration is required and which activities and locations it covers.

title: Mortgage company renewal report
summary: The statute specifies an annual renewal and a prescribed report accompanying the renewal fee for mortgage brokers and lenders.
evidence: License expiration, current commissioner instructions, required report and renewal receipt.
counsel: Reconcile the statutory renewal timing with current NMLS workflow and confirm the report contents and route.

title: Wyoming reports of condition
summary: Wyoming requires reports of condition in the form and with the information the registry requires.
evidence: License, current form and calendar, reconciled report and receipt.
counsel: Confirm current FV7 sections, no-activity treatment and how to keep evidence separate from the renewal report.

title: Mortgage broker or lender company authority
authority: AS 06.60 and Alaska Division of Banking and Securities guidance
summary: The division describes mortgage broker or lender authority and individual originator licensing under Alaska's mortgage regime.
evidence: Company and branch authority, role, individual sponsorship and any exemption basis.
counsel: Confirm which activities, offices and exemptions are in scope and whether another consumer finance license is relevant.

title: Alaska annual broker or lender attestation
authority: AS 06.60.100 and Alaska annual report form
summary: The state form describes a March 15 prior-calendar-year filing in NMLS under oath or affirmation and references the MCR submission.
evidence: Current form, license and year, attested activity and associated MCR evidence, submission receipt.
counsel: Confirm that the current report year uses this form and upload route, and how no-activity or cessation is handled.

title: Alaska NMLS reports of condition
authority: AS 06.60.100(c) and Alaska Division of Banking and Securities enforcement order
summary: The division identifies quarterly call report duties under Alaska law and treats them separately from annual filings in its published enforcement order.
evidence: Entity and authority, current FV7 form and calendar, reconciled workpaper and receipt.
counsel: Confirm current form and reporting obligations, including separate fiscal or annual state evidence.

title: Mortgage loan originator company authority
authority: HRS ch. 454F and Hawaii DFI mortgage originator FAQ
summary: DFI distinguishes mortgage loan originator companies, individuals and exempt sponsoring companies for residential origination activity.
evidence: Company authority or approved exemption, locations, individuals and sponsorship evidence.
counsel: Confirm which company and individual authorization applies, including exemptions and office requirements.

title: Mortgage call reports for covered licensees and sponsors
summary: Hawaii addresses quarterly reports of condition for licensees and exempt sponsoring companies where required under federal law, in the NMLS-prescribed form.
evidence: Company and sponsorship status, current quarter and form, reconciled figures and filing receipt.
counsel: Confirm current FV7 schedules and sections and any financial or no-activity requirements for the actual entity.

title: DRE Mortgage Loan Disclosure Statement and delivery timing
summary: The DRE broker statute ties delivery to the earlier of three business days after a completed written application or the borrower becoming obligated on the note. It prescribes content and recognizes a conditional alternative.
evidence: DRE authority, loan type and principal amount, completed written application and note obligation times, signed disclosure and delivery.
counsel: Confirm covered products and thresholds, approved form or alternative, translated materials and overlap with TRID.

title: DRE license numbers and originator identifiers in advertising
summary: DRE describes display of the broker license number and applicable originator NMLS ID and distinguishes media and solicitation types.
evidence: Published creative and channel, DRE and NMLS identifiers, capacity and claims support, and approval evidence.
counsel: Confirm exact identifiers, prominent display and medium and audience exceptions.

title: DRE mortgage records and inspection access
summary: DRE requires broker transaction records and the signed mortgage disclosure or applicable alternative, with a three-year retention requirement and records available for inspection.
evidence: Executed and obtained documents, signed disclosure and delivery, disposition and dates, and examination retrieval.
counsel: Confirm the retention start, unconsummated files, any trust records and longer applicable retention.

title: Accuracy of borrower loan terms for CFL licensees
summary: DFPI cites the CFL prohibition on materially false or misleading borrower representations about loan terms or conditions when making or brokering a loan.
evidence: CFL authority and counterparty, dated representations and offers, loan terms and any correction.
counsel: Confirm CFL scope, permitted counterparties, material changes requiring notice and other borrower disclosures.

title: CFL advertising identifier and advertising copy
summary: The adopted rules address unique identifiers in mortgage ads, a limited-character electronic ad link exception, and advertising copy retention, including originator ads kept by the sponsor.
evidence: Creative, channel and character limit, linked destination, sponsor and identifiers, publication and last-use dates.
counsel: Confirm operative rule and exact short-format exception, claim requirements and retention.

title: CFL books, records and independent escrow evidence
summary: The CFL requires compliance records and addresses records for real-property secured loans disbursed through independent escrow.
evidence: CFL license, books and loan file inventory, escrow evidence, storage and examination production.
counsel: Confirm current underlying regulations, which files and records are required, and retention and location.

title: DRE company mortgage call reports
authority: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §10166.08; DRE SAFE Act guidance
summary: DRE identifies company MCR filing obligations for its mortgage loan origination endorsement program.
evidence: Company license and endorsement, filed period and components, reconciled activity or no activity and NMLS receipt.
counsel: Confirm covered endorsement, current filing schedule and distinction from threshold broker and DFPI reports.

title: Preclosing disclosure under Oregon mortgage broker law
summary: The statute requires the mortgage banker or broker to supply the borrower with the referenced federal real estate lending disclosure before closing.
evidence: Covered loan and broker role, applicable disclosure version, dated delivery and closing evidence.
counsel: Resolve current federal equivalent and product and party scope given the statute's older Regulation Z citation.

title: Mortgage advertising identity and archive by channel
summary: Oregon lists print, broadcast and electronic advertising records, including covered mobile app versions. Related rules address licensee identity and identifiers.
evidence: Published creative and scripts, app version where applicable, publication dates, approved name and identifiers.
counsel: Confirm advertisement categories, archive period and identifiers by medium.

title: Residential borrower files and disposition evidence
summary: The borrower file rule lists signed applications and identifiers, fee agreements when prepared, applicable rate lock or float evidence and disposition records.
evidence: Executed application, ID and signatures, loan file and status, fee and rate records and exam retrieval.
counsel: Confirm form and retention by disposition, storage, review of signatures and longer applicable periods.

title: Oregon NMLS residential mortgage reports of condition
summary: The rule specifies filing through NMLS within 45 days after each calendar quarter and describes its license and activity period using preceding-calendar-year language.
evidence: License dates, period-specific form instructions, state activity reconciliation, submission and amendment receipts.
counsel: Confirm how the rule's period wording applies to the quarter, no-activity treatment and relationship to the statutory annual report.

title: Broker disclosures after application or receipt of funds
summary: The rule sets a three-business-day window tied to receipt of a loan application or third-party service money. It requires copies and the lender agreement if a lender provides disclosures.
evidence: Dated application and funds receipts, applicable fee and summary disclosures, delivery, and lender agreement where used.
counsel: Confirm state triggers and exceptions, accepted forms and responsibilities, and overlap with federal timing and fee rules.

title: Advertised rates, APR prominence and rate evidence
summary: Washington addresses advertised rate availability, APR prominence, prohibited claims and use of current loan information. The broker retains a rate sheet or other rate support and APR calculation for specific advertised rates.
evidence: Published ad, lender rate sheet or equivalent, APR calculation, distribution and approval.
counsel: Confirm channel-specific disclosures, source wording and required identifiers and evidence.

title: Covered preclosing fees and third-party costs
summary: The statute limits preclosing charges to listed categories, including actually incurred costs for third-party services rendered, and requires reasonable and customary charges.
evidence: Charge category, invoice and service date, fee and approval and closing events, plus cancellation or refund evidence.
counsel: Confirm origination or modification scope, exceptions and the effect of federal fee timing.

title: Accessible loan and originator records
summary: The statute requires records in the United States that the director can access, addresses preservation after the final loan entry and separately covers records of originator relationships.
evidence: File and final entry, location and access sample, dated sponsorship or employment records and exam response.
counsel: Confirm the exact retention period and starts for each record category, including longer federal requirements.

title: Idaho quarterly mortgage call report
summary: Licensed mortgage brokers and lenders submit quarterly mortgage call reports through NMLS within 45 days after the quarter ends.
evidence: License, applicable quarter, reconciled activity or zero activity, prescribed component and receipt.
counsel: Confirm scope, exact fields, supplements and treatment of periods with no activity.

title: Idaho annual report of financial condition
summary: The statute specifies an annual financial-condition report through NMLS within 45 days after calendar year end. The director prescribes form and content.
evidence: Company and annual period, regulator instructions, financial component and receipt.
counsel: Confirm current filing instructions and reconcile the statutory timing with NMLS component instructions before scheduling a legal deadline.

title: Montana broker origination disclosure
summary: The agency identifies its required state disclosure at application before providing broker services, with borrower signature.
evidence: Application and service chronology, operative disclosure and borrower signature, copy and delivery evidence.
counsel: Confirm trigger, form version, party scope and acceptable signatures and delivery.

title: Licensee name, NMLS identifier and Consumer Access link
summary: The division identifies name and NMLS identifier requirements for covered advertisements and a link to the broker's NMLS Consumer Access page on the website.
evidence: Published ad and channel, approved name and identifier, website link and dated approval.
counsel: Confirm identities by channel, applicable digital rules and any rate-sheet support.

title: Mortgage pipeline and five-year loan file access
summary: The division requires an application pipeline and five-year retention from the last file activity. A broker relying on the lender's system must preserve access after the relationship ends.
evidence: Pipeline and statuses, file contents and dated last activity, custody and independent retrieval sample.
counsel: Confirm file content and exact start for each disposition, access after termination and longer obligations.

title: Signed broker agreement and advance delivery
summary: The statute ties the signed agreement to three business days after the borrower signs a completed application and requires delivery before consideration. It addresses required contents and fee increases.
evidence: Completed application and signature, agreement and delivery, consideration, itemized fees and changed-fee explanation.
counsel: Confirm business-day and consideration definitions, which fee changes require redisclosure, and treatment of legacy federal form references.

title: Mortgage advertising claims and originator identification
summary: Wyoming prohibits false promises and misrepresentations through advertising and addresses unique identifiers on covered originator applications, solicitations and ads.
evidence: Published creative, lender rate support, originator and company identifiers and approval.
counsel: Confirm which act and identifier rule apply to the entity, activity and medium.

title: Loan records and out-of-state examination access
summary: Wyoming requires closing-related loan records for 25 months from closing and addresses production when records are outside the state.
evidence: Closed file inventory and date, records location, request and delivery or examination expense evidence.
counsel: Confirm applicable record types, unclosed files and longer requirements.

title: Borrower permission and written amount for co-broker fee
summary: Alaska's unfair-practices rule addresses a broker engaging another broker who will charge the borrower an additional fee. It requires advance written permission and the fee amount in writing.
evidence: Broker roles, fee amount and dated written permission, engagement and collection events.
counsel: Confirm current rule text, applicable actors, when permission is required and federal fee restrictions.

summary: Alaska prohibits false, misleading or deceptive representations concerning mortgage rates, terms or conditions.
evidence: Published dated material, substantiation and contemporaneous rate or terms, approval and role evidence.
counsel: Confirm the operative statute and separate identifier, medium and archive rules.

authority: AS 06.60.135; Alaska Division of Banking examination enforcement
summary: Alaska requires mortgage records and has enforced timely production of complete loan files. The agency's examination order also addresses separating business records.

counsel: Confirm scope for broker and lender files, current retention and production deadline, and out-of-state storage.

summary: Hawaii prohibits covered best-efforts agreements allowing compensation when the borrower obtains no loan and requires applicable disclosures. The statute addresses handling of amounts or documents the licensee cannot retain.
evidence: Agreement and terms, loan outcome, compensation or refund, and dated disclosure evidence.
counsel: Confirm current role, contract and fee scope and separate state and federal disclosure duties.

title: Originator identifier and advertising claims
summary: Hawaii requires the originator's unique identifier on covered applications, solicitations and advertising, including business cards and websites. It separately addresses unavailable terms and misleading claims.
evidence: Published material, application, unique identifier and exemption facts, dated term and claim evidence.
counsel: Confirm covered roles and any company identifiers or channel rules.

title: Loan records and regulator examination production
summary: The commissioner can request loan books, files and records, require reports and obtain access for an examination or investigation.
evidence: Records inventory and file samples, regulator request and dated production, role and access evidence.
